title: Open neighborhood in a specialization-invariant subset
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-sober topological space with finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Let $E\subseteq X$ satisfy $x\in E\Longleftrightarrow y\in E$ whenever $x\rightsquigarrow y$. For every $x\in E$ there is an open subset $V$ such that $x\in V\subseteq E$. Here quasi-sobriety means that every irreducible closed subset has a generic point; no uniqueness or $T_0$ hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 0GKC, component-shrinking paragraph, its purely topological argument

proof.text: Remove the union of the irreducible components not containing x. Each component is closed and the union is finite, so its complement V is open and contains x.

source.place: Tag 0GKC, component-shrinking paragraph, its purely topological argument

proof.text: For y in V choose an irreducible component containing y. It also contains x, since otherwise it was removed. Its generic point specializes to both x and y; invariance first transfers membership from x to the generic point, then to y. Thus V is contained in E.

theorem exists_open_subset_of_specialization_invariant
    {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [QuasiSober X]
    (hfin : (irreducibleComponents X).Finite) (E : Set X)
    (hE : ∀ x y : X, x ⤳ y → (x ∈ E ↔ y ∈ E))
    (x : X) (hx : x ∈ E) :
    ∃ V : TopologicalSpace.Opens X, x ∈ V ∧ (V : Set X) ⊆ E
